tasks.name: reverse_words
tests: assert reverse_words('a b  c') == 'c b a'
turns: Write a Python function reverse_words(s) that returns the words of s in reverse order joined by single spaces, treating any whitespace run as a separator. Reply with a single Python code block containing only the function (and any helpers), no prints and no tests.

tasks.name: balanced
turns: Write a Python function balanced(s) that returns True if the brackets ()[]{} in s are balanced and properly nested, ignoring other characters, else False. Reply with a single Python code block containing only the function (and any helpers), no prints and no tests.

tasks.name: two_sum
turns: Write a Python function two_sum(nums, target) that returns a tuple (i, j) with i < j and nums[i] + nums[j] == target, the lexicographically smallest such pair, or None. Reply with a single Python code block containing only the function (and any helpers), no prints and no tests.

tasks.name: rle
turns: Write a Python function rle(s) that run-length encodes s as pairs, e.g. rle('aaab') returns [('a', 3), ('b', 1)]; rle('') returns []. Reply with a single Python code block containing only the function (and any helpers), no prints and no tests.

tasks.name: is_prime
tests: assert is_prime(2) and is_prime(97) and is_prime(7919)
assert not is_prime(1) and not is_prime(0) and not is_prime(-7)
assert not is_prime(91) and not is_prime(1000)
turns: Write a Python function is_prime(n) that returns True for prime integers n >= 2 and False otherwise (including n < 2). Reply with a single Python code block containing only the function (and any helpers), no prints and no tests.

tasks.name: transpose
turns: Write a Python function transpose(m) that returns the transpose of a rectangular list-of-lists matrix m (a list of lists); transpose([]) returns []. Reply with a single Python code block containing only the function (and any helpers), no prints and no tests.

tasks.name: group_anagrams
